answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The ledge multiplier is published, charged in jetty, and fable lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3341 identities would post 3316 proofs and burn roughly 43 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
